sources.cite: AWS IAM User Guide, 'AWS: Denies access to AWS based on the requested Region'
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'Actions in the CloudFront, IAM, Route 53, and Support services should not be denied because these are popular AWS global services with a single endpoint that is physically located in the us-east-1 Region ... the requests would be denied without the NotAction element'; the example's NotAction lists cloudfront, iam, organizations, route53 and support, and the page says to extend it for other global services you use (budgets, globalaccelerator, waf ...). The page covers identity policies; The AWS Organizations page 'SCP evaluation' (read 2026-11-18): a deny in any SCP from the root through the OUs to the account applies to everything beneath it and no allow can override it; an action is allowed only if every level allows it, so SCPs set the maximum available permissions and grant nothing to users or roles themselves. The CloudTrail message in the case is an authored rendering.
